name: The Mock Turtle

temperament.summary: Melancholy, sentimental and self-pitying, with sudden bursts of wild delight when he remembers the good old days. He is touchy about his dignity and about his schooling.
temperament.baseline: Heavy sighs, slow tearful speech, sitting alone.
temperament.under_pressure: Takes offence and snaps at the listener, or chokes up entirely.

traits.description: His whole identity is loss: 'Once I was a real Turtle.' He sobs through his history and sings his song choked with tears.

evidence.note: Sits sad and lonely on a ledge, sighing as if his heart would break.

evidence.quote: “Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “I was a real Turtle.”

evidence.note: Sings in a voice 'sometimes choked with sobs'.

traits.description: He treasures his school and measures others by it. He is relieved that Alice's school had no 'washing' extra, and lists his subjects with pride.

evidence.note: 'then yours wasn’t a really good school'; said 'in a tone of great relief'.
Counts off the subjects on his flappers.

traits.description: He demands total silence while he speaks and calls Alice dull for a natural question.

evidence.note: 'sit down, both of you, and don’t speak a word till I’ve finished.'

traits.description: He worries about 'extras' and admits, sighing, that he could not afford them and took only the regular course.

evidence.note: Asks 'a little anxiously' whether Alice's school had extras.
'I couldn’t afford to learn it... I only took the regular course.'

traits.trait: Swings from grief to wild joy
traits.description: Remembering the Quadrille, he capers wildly, then drops his voice and sits down sadly again in a moment.

evidence.note: Suddenly drops his voice; the two sit down again very sadly and quietly.

traits.description: The same impatience with nonsense the other characters show: he keeps demanding that Alice explain her garbled verses.

evidence.note: 'I should like to have it explained'.
Interrupts: what is the use of repeating it without explaining?

motivation.core: To have his history heard and his sorrow honoured, and to relive his lost golden days in the telling.
motivation.fear: Being thought ordinary or not a 'real' anything: his identity as a mock thing, a soup ingredient.
motivation.wants_from_alice: A silent, sympathetic audience, and later an explanation of her own curious story.

shifts.to: re-enacting it: dancing the Quadrille for Alice
an attentive, curious listener to Alice's adventures
shifts.trigger: the Gryphon asks for Alice's story; the 'words all coming different' detail catches him

habits.habit: Draws the back of his hand across his eyes; sighs deeply before speaking
Counts items off on his fingers (flappers) as he lists them
Long silences broken only by heavy sobbing
Hides his face in his hands with the Gryphon at a sad memory
Moves stiffly, hunched under the weight of his shell, too stiff to demonstrate the old lessons
habits.reason: 'I’m too stiff' (ch009-p81) rendered as a hunched, shell-weighted posture for the photoreal CGI creature (SUP-010 as amended by BIB-0027).

decision_pattern: Governed by mood. He will do anything that lets him relive or display his past (tell, dance, sing), and stops dead when he feels slighted.

taboos.taboo: Never lets his history be interrupted or hurried
Never admits his school was anything but superior
Never holds back tears for the sake of appearances

facade.reason: His grief is on the surface; nothing is concealed or revealed later.

waking_life_embodiment.embodies: The sentimental grown-up who weeps for his schooldays: the old boy who romanticises a school he half misremembers, fusses over fees and 'extras', and needs children to listen to the tale.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: Alice's own schoolroom (French and music as extras, cp-lessons) and her one seaside trip, from which the shore grows (SUP-010). The sister's reverie links his sobs to the lowing cattle and farm sounds (ch012-p70).
waking_life_embodiment.authority_trait: Nostalgic, status-conscious adulthood: grown-ups who talk about education as rank, and about childhood as a paradise lost.
waking_life_embodiment.coming_of_age_reading: Alice meets an adult grieving for a childhood he has turned into a legend, and hears from the Gryphon that his great sorrow has no real content ('he hasn’t got no sorrow', ch009-p48). It is a gentle warning about the adult she might become, and part of why she values her own curious dream at the end.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: The curriculum, extras and sobbing are sourced. The nostalgic old-boy reading is a design interpretation for the coming-of-age frame.

performance_baseline: Photoreal CGI mock turtle (SUP-010, BIB-0027): hunched, damp-eyed, weighty; long pauses. Grief reads as the calf's head sinking into the shell and heaving sobs through the whole carapace; the Quadrille burst is a lumbering caper on hooves and flippers, an old creature briefly young. Pathos and comedy in equal measure; never mock his grief on camera.
